reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

votes.question: On Passage — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This bill authorizes fiscal year 2027 military programs, troop levels, and related Energy Department national-security work. A Yea passes it in the House. A Nay votes against passage.

votes.question: On Motion to Recommit — National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: The fiscal year 2027 defense bill sets military policy, troop levels, and related Energy Department security programs. This vote would have sent that bill back to the Armed Services Committee with no rewrite attached. A Yea would have pulled it off the floor; a Nay left it up for the passage vote.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment would have required the Defense Secretary to report options for cutting the department's civilian workforce by 200,000. A Yea would have added that report. A Nay voted not to add it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to the fiscal year 2027 defense bill would ban automated speed-enforcement cameras on military bases. A Yea adds that ban to the bill. A Nay leaves the bill without it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have let the Secretary approve any eligible investor and cleared investment professional who meets the program's requirements to assess investment opportunities matching the department's needs, with no cap on participants, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment codifies protections and responsibilities for chaplains and subjects such protections to prosecution under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to authorize the Secretary of Defense to establish a school choice pilot program for members of the Armed Forces.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits male participation in female sports at Department of Defense Education Activity schools.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment prohibits gender-related medical care under TRICARE and prevents TRICARE from covering certain gender-related medical procedures and treatments.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have codified Executive Order 14183, which requires all personnel to serve in accordance with their biological sex, according to the Congressional Research Service description. A Yea supports adopting it; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment establishes a presumption of approval for qualified Department of Defense servicemembers and civilian employees seeking authorization from their facility commander to carry personal firearms on military installations.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “An amendment numbered 15 printed in Part A of House Report 119-755 to prohibit funds for Ukraine Security Assistance except for U.S. embassy security in Ukraine.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to prohibit the Department of Defense from using taxpayer funds to cover the costs of foreign military personnel participating in bilateral or multilateral military exercises conducted with the United States unless the Secretary of Defense waives the prohibition when necessary to support a U.S. national security interest.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to preempt state and local laws that impose requirements different from federal standards on certain defense-related recycling, disposal, and materials recovery activities.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)

votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) would have barred courts from issuing injunctions that impair military readiness, military fuel supply, or defense-related logistical support, according to the Congressional Research Service description. votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment strikes section 518, relating to the pilot program on modernization of drug testing using voice-based risk assessment technology to identify servicemembers for drug testing.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.question: On Agreeing to the Amendment (H R 8800)
votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 524, which removes the existing statutory limit on the number of cadets who may receive alternative service obligations to pursue professional athletic careers, thereby preserving the current cap.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027
votes.plain_language: This amendment to H.R. 8800 (National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027) is summarized by the Congressional Research Service as: “Amendment sought to strike section 521 and replace it with a prohibition on foreign nationals attending the United States Military Academies.” A Yea supports adding it to the bill; a Nay opposes it.

votes.bill_title: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027

posts.text:
Every American outside of the richest 1% is paying more as a result of Donald Trump’s tax and economic policies.

Families across the Sacramento region deserve better. 

That's why I'm fighting in Congress to bring down costs, make our tax code fairer, and build an economy that

I was asked earlier this week by CNN if I thought the Trump administration was abandoning Ukraine.  

Trump’s decision to waive new sanctions on Russia should leave no doubt: that is exactly what is happening.  

My Republican colleagues pushed hard to pass the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill before we left town. They ought to be standing up and screaming at the top of their lungs that we don't side with Russia.  

We must stand with the Ukrainian people.

Trump’s diesel deal gives Vladimir Putin millions of dollars to finance his war against the Ukrainian people while doing next to nothing to lower prices at the pump. 
 
This dangerous and irresponsible decision must be reversed.
 
That’s why I joined 17 of my colleagues in introducing bipartisan legislation to block it.

I was proud to recognize Ismael Pantoja, owner of Cantina Azteca in Carmichael, with our October Small Business of the Month award!

For the past decade, Cantina Azteca has shared the flavors and traditions of Mexico with our community, bringing families, friends, and neighbors together through great food and hospitality.

As Hispanic Heritage Month comes to a close, I'm grateful for local businesses like Cantina Azteca that enrich the cultural fabric of our community. 

Congratulations to Ismael and the entire Cantina Azteca team on this well-deserved recognition!

Ukrainians continue to fight admirably to defend their own country.

We have to do everything we can to support the Ukrainian people — not betray them and take the side of Vladimir Putin. https://t.co/WBGuNZdQ5B

I’m horrified to learn that Congressman Krishnamoorthi and his family were worshipping when a white supremacist attempted a mass shooting targeting Indian Americans.

This incident is a stark reminder of the threats facing Hindu communities and other communities targeted by religious and racial hatred.

Every American has the right to worship in peace. Congress must do more to combat hate-fueled violence and protect our communities from these threats.

Trump's war with Iran is driving energy prices higher and his tariffs are making everyday goods more expensive.  We must bring this war to an end and reverse Trump’s tariffs to lower costs for American families. https://t.co/88h8jdcZsQ

Know an outstanding educator in our community? 

Nominate them to be our next Educator of the Month: https://t.co/uZrWi8Zs10

It was an honor to recognize Evelyn Margolin of Cameron Ranch Elementary School in Carmichael as our October Educator of the Month!

For 25 years, Evelyn served as a special education teacher in the San Juan Unified School District. Throughout her career, she championed inclusive education, supported families, and helped ensure students of all abilities had the opportunity to succeed.

Even in retirement, she continues to give back through Margolin’s Garden of Learning, a garden she founded where she teaches weekly lessons in science, nutrition, and environmental stewardship to students from transitional kindergarten through fifth grade.

As the son of a public school teacher, I know firsthand the lasting impact that dedicated educators have on our children and communities. 

Thank you, Evelyn, for your decades of service and continued commitment to the next generation of learners!

Trump’s war with Iran is driving up gas and diesel prices, fueling inflation, and raising costs for families across the Sacramento region.

The impact goes far beyond the gas pump. Higher fuel prices make it more expensive to produce and transport goods, increase operating costs for businesses, and ultimately drive up prices on everyday essentials.

We must end this reckless war and bring down costs for the American people.
https://t.co/MoPjPukR2U

Janine and I had a great time at the California Capital Airshow this weekend at Mather Airport!

The Sacramento region has a proud history of aviation and military service. This year’s airshow celebrated that legacy, honored our veterans and service members, and inspired the next generation of aviators, engineers, and STEM innovators.

Congratulations to Darcy Brewer and the entire California Capital Airshow team on 20 years of bringing this incredible event to our region!

On Indigenous Peoples’ Day, we celebrate the rich history, culture, and contributions of Native peoples in Sacramento County and across our nation.

Sacramento County is the proud home of Wilton Rancheria, our county’s only federally recognized tribe.

Under the leadership of my friend and Sacramento native Chairman Jesus Tarango, the tribe continues to preserve its heritage, strengthen our local economy, and serve as an important partner in our community.

I’m grateful for Chairman Tarango’s leadership and look forward to our continued efforts to strengthen our region for generations to come.

Public executions are the hallmark of oppressive regimes, not free democracies.

This latest display of deeply disturbing judgment from Secretary Hegseth only strengthens the case for Congress to hold him accountable. https://t.co/gFMMwNNlTe

For 25 years, the Regional Water Authority has brought together water providers and affiliates across the greater Sacramento region to strengthen the reliability, quality, and affordability of our water supply for the 2.2 million people they serve.

Their work has helped residents use water more efficiently and supported major investments in groundwater storage to strengthen our region’s long-term water resilience.

I was honored to join the RWA’s 25th anniversary celebration in Sacramento to present Executive Director Jim Peifer with a Congressional Record statement recognizing this important milestone.

Congratulations to the Regional Water Authority on 25 years of regional leadership and service to our community!

I had the honor of recognizing Bob McGarvey as my office’s October Veteran of the Month yesterday at Rancho Cordova City Hall.

Bob served our nation in the Air Force from 1961 to 1967, including two and a half years of active duty at Mather Air Force Base and two years in the Air Force Reserve. 

That commitment has continued through decades of service to Rancho Cordova in local schools, civic organizations, and community life.

Thank you, Bob, for your service to our nation and for your dedication to making Rancho Cordova a great place to live. 

Congratulations on this well-deserved recognition!

Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar and the passengers and crew who rushed the cockpit aboard Flight 1073 showed extraordinary courage in the face of unimaginable terror.

Their heroism saved more than 170 lives on board and averted an even greater tragedy on the ground. 

I am grateful to Captain Machchhar, the passengers, and the crew on board for their bravery and quick action.

My District Chief of Staff Matt Ceccato was honored to join the return ceremony for the Sacramento-based 319th Expeditionary Signal Battalion following the battalion’s deployment during the Iran war.

Throughout their deployment, these Soldiers carried out a demanding mission, maintaining critical communications across multiple countries under difficult conditions.

At the ceremony, Matt had the privilege of recognizing six Purple Heart recipients on my behalf and presented each of them with a congressional challenge coin.

We owe an enduring debt of gratitude to these brave men and women in uniform, and to the families who supported them throughout their deployment. 

Welcome home, and thank you for your service and sacrifice to our nation. 🇺🇸

I welcome Xi Jinping’s invitation for 100,000 American students to visit and study in China.   As Co-Chair of the Congressional International Exchanges Caucus, I believe educational and cultural exchanges are an important way to build mutual understanding and expertise.  But those exchanges depend on trust and the ability to study, speak, and engage without fear of harassment or arbitrary detention. 

Right now, American scholar Min Zin remains wrongfully detained in China, and Beijing continues to target scholars, human rights advocates, and diaspora communities whose work or speech it finds unwelcome.   If President Xi wants more Americans to study in China, releasing Min Zin would be an important first step toward creating the conditions that make genuine cultural and educational exchange possible between our two nations.

My previous run-in with @thecapitolfox wasn’t a fun experience, but I was fortunate to have access to readily available and low-cost rabies vaccines. 

But for far too many Americans, an unfortunate run-in like mine could break the bank.

That’s why I introduced legislation last Congress to lower the costs of rabies vaccines for uninsured individuals. 

High costs should never be a barrier for individuals seeking life-saving treatment.
Thank God I’m in Sacramento https://t.co/Xofadphest

The wrongful detention of U.S. citizens by the PRC demonstrates the serious risks Americans face when their work is deemed sensitive by Beijing.

During last week’s @HouseForeign hearing, we welcomed Min Zin’s spouse, Sylvia, and discussed Beijing’s repression of human rights advocates, scholars, and minority communities.

As President Trump meets with Xi Jinping, I’m urging him to raise these concerns directly and press for the release of Min Zin and Youlin Chen.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
